what_it_is.prose: Aviadvigatel (JSC Aviadvigatel, Perm), the successor to the Soloviev design bureau and now part of Russia's United Engine Corporation (Rostec), is the design house behind the D-30 family of turbofans. The D-30KP variant powers the Indian Air Force's Ilyushin Il-76MD 'Gajraj' heavy-lifters and Il-78MKI tankers (four engines per aircraft). Aviadvigatel is also the developer of the more modern PS-90A-76 turbofan, which Russia has proposed to re-engine India's ageing Il-76 fleet in place of the D-30KP. India's exposure to Aviadvigatel is therefore the Il-76 engine dependency — D-30KP supply, spares and overhaul, and any future PS-90A-76 re-engining — a dependency strained by the Russia-Ukraine war. This is a compact (Tier C) card: as a foreign engine supplier, the firm's documented India footprint is essentially the Il-76 powerplant link, with the PS-90 re-engine still at proposal/study stage and no Indian production or JV established.

variant: Tier C compact card (Il-76 engine supplier)
open_questions: Whether India will contract the PS-90A-76 re-engine for the Il-76, and on what terms, is not settled.
Extent of continued D-30KP spares/overhaul support to India during the war is unclear.
